product.howItWorks.title: How It Works
product.howItWorks.intro: Conventional insulation resists heat conduction. TC101 reflects radiant heat.
product.howItWorks.step1.title: Ceramic microspheres
product.howItWorks.step1.description: Hollow ceramic spheres in a latex binder. Microsphere walls reflect infrared radiation like tiny mirrors. Heat isn't absorbed – it's bounced back.
product.howItWorks.step2.title: Reflection instead of absorption
product.howItWorks.step2.description: Most industrial heat transfers by radiation. TC101 doesn't absorb or resist heat – it reflects it outright. That's why a millimeter coating works where mineral wool needs inches.
product.howItWorks.step3.title: Thin-film application
product.howItWorks.step3.description: Applied like ordinary paint – by brush, roller, or spray. No scaffolding, no disassembly, minimal downtime. Application takes minutes instead of days.

product.advantages.fireResistant.title: Fire resistant
product.advantages.fireResistant.descrip: Ceramic base withstands temperatures up to 260 °C. Won't burn, won't release toxic gases, meets fire safety standards.
product.advantages.lightweight.title: Extremely lightweight
product.advantages.lightweight.descripti: A 1mm coating weighs a fraction of conventional insulation. Structures carry less load and last longer.
product.advantages.antiCorrosion.title: Prevents corrosion under insulation (CUI)
product.advantages.antiCorrosion.descrip: Breathable material releases condensation and prevents corrosion under insulation – a common cause of industrial failures.
product.advantages.vaporPermeable.title: Vapor permeable
product.advantages.vaporPermeable.descri: Material breathes – doesn't trap moisture or create water pockets. Extends the life of insulated structures.
product.advantages.flexible.title: Flexible
product.advantages.flexible.description: Up to 80% elongation – covers bends, elbows, valves. Won't crack during thermal expansion.
product.advantages.wideTemp.title: Wide temperature range

faq.meta.title: Frequently Asked Questions about TC101 | Union B+C
faq.meta.description: Answers to questions about application, technical specifications, maintenance, and safety of TEMP-COAT TC101 liquid ceramic insulation.
faq.page.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.page.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about TC101
faq.where_used.question: Where is TC101 used?
faq.where_used.answer: TC101 replaces or supplements conventional insulation systems in industry and construction. It's used wherever you need to control surface temperature, prevent burns, eliminate condensation, or limit heat transfer. Typical applications: steam and hot media piping, tanks, boilers, heat exchangers, industrial halls, roofs, facades.
faq.how_much.question: How much material do I need per square meter?
faq.how_much.answer: Consumption depends on the required coating thickness. At the recommended 0.5 mm per coat, you'll need about 0.34 kg per m². For burn protection, 1–2 mm total thickness (2–4 coats) is usually sufficient. For thermal insulation, apply 2–4 mm (4–8 coats). We have calculation tables based on surface temperature.
faq.application_method.question: How is TC101 applied?
faq.application_method.answer: Applied like regular paint: by brush, roller, or airless spray equipment. For small areas, a brush is sufficient. For large applications, we recommend an airless gun with a 0.43–0.53 mm (17–21 thou) tip and 150–200 bar pressure. Material is ready to use—do not mix with thinners. Stir thoroughly before application.
faq.layer_thickness.question: How thick can I apply in one coat?
faq.layer_thickness.answer: Maximum 0.5 mm per coat. Thicker coats dry slowly and may crack. If you need greater thickness, apply multiple thin coats. Each subsequent coat is applied once the previous one is dry to the touch (typically 1–2 hours at 24 °C).
faq.primer.question: Do I need a primer?
faq.primer.answer: On steel, yes—use any anti-corrosion primer (epoxy, alkyd, zinc dust). TC101 contains water, which would cause rust on bare steel. On aluminum, stainless steel, galvanized metal, and concrete, TC101 is applied directly without a primer. Surface must be clean, dry, and degreased.
faq.temp_range.question: What temperature range does TC101 work in?
faq.temp_range.answer: Certified range is -60 °C to +260 °C (short-term peak). For continuous operation, we recommend a maximum of +200 °C. Material is classified Class E per EN 13501-1 – does not spread flame.
faq.expansion.question: Will the coating withstand thermal expansion?
faq.expansion.answer: Yes. Elongation reaches up to 80%, so the coating follows substrate movement without cracking. This is crucial on pipes that change dimensions when heated. Conventional rigid insulation would crack or detach. TC101 remains flexible even at low temperatures.
faq.weight.question: How much does the coating weigh after application?
faq.weight.answer: A 1 mm coating weighs about 0.65 kg/m². That's a fraction of conventional insulation weight (mineral wool, polystyrene). For example, a 3 mm coating weighs under 2 kg/m², while conventional insulation with the same insulating effect can weigh 10–50 kg/m². Therefore, TC101 doesn't stress structures and is suitable even for light beams or old piping.
faq.drying_time.question: How long does one coat take to dry?
faq.drying_time.answer: At 24 °C, the coating is dry to the touch in 1 hour. You can apply the next coat in 2–4 hours, once the previous one is completely dry (shouldn't smear). Full cure is reached in 24–48 hours. In cold weather, drying takes longer; in heat (above 27 °C), it's faster. Do not apply below 5 °C or in humid conditions.
faq.cleaning.question: How is the coating cleaned?
faq.cleaning.answer: TC101 surface has a microporous structure, so it can trap dust. Clean with pressurized water (pressure washer) or soapy solution with a cloth. In heavily soiled environments, we recommend applying a top acrylic coating to seal the surface and simplify maintenance. Oil, diesel, or gas won't damage the coating—remove any stains with a cloth dampened with acetone.
faq.shelf_life.question: How long does unopened material last?
faq.shelf_life.answer: Warranty period is 12 months from manufacture when stored in a dry, cool place (5–25 °C). Protect from freezing. Even two-year-old material may be usable if it hasn't separated and has no odor. Always stir thoroughly before use.
faq.curing.question: How long does curing take?
faq.curing.answer: Full cure is reached in 24–72 hours depending on thickness and conditions. If you plan a top coat, wait at least 48 hours. If you apply to a hot surface (up to 100 °C), curing is faster. For surfaces above 100 °C, follow special instructions in the manual.
faq.protection.question: What protective equipment is needed?
faq.protection.answer: TC101 is water-based and non-toxic. In enclosed spaces, use standard protection as for painting: gloves, work clothes, respirator when spraying. In open areas, a dust mask is sufficient. Material contains no heavy metals or toxic solvents. On skin contact, wash with water. If eyes are affected, rinse with water for 15 minutes and seek medical attention.
faq.flammable.question: Is TC101 flammable?
faq.flammable.answer: TC101 is classified as reaction to fire Class E per EN 13501-1 – it does not spread flame. It can be applied near heat sources or during operation. Material withstands temperatures up to 260 °C without degradation. Does not release toxic smoke gases. Meets fire regulations for industrial applications.
faq.certification.question: Is TC101 certified in the Czech Republic?
faq.certification.answer: Yes. We have a product conformity certificate according to Czech and European standards. Material has been tested for thermal conductivity, fire resistance, elongation, and durability. A safety data sheet is available according to REACH regulation. All certificates can be found in the Certificates section.
faq.materials.question: What materials is TC101 suitable for?
faq.materials.answer: TC101 adheres to most construction and industrial surfaces: steel (with anti-corrosion primer), stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized metal, concrete, plaster, wood, glass, PVC, polyester. Not suitable for silicones and polyethylene (weak adhesion). Before application, surface must be clean, dry, and degreased. On glossy surfaces, we recommend light sanding for better adhesion.

guide.title: TC101 Application Guide
guide.intro: Follow these steps to achieve optimal insulating effect and coating durability.
guide.step1.title: Surface Preparation
guide.step1.description: Surface must be clean, dry, and degreased. Remove old coatings, rust, grease, and dust. On steel, apply anti-corrosion primer (epoxy, alkyd, zinc dust). Let dry according to primer instructions. On stainless steel, aluminum, galvanized metal, and concrete, primer is not necessary – just degrease and dry.
guide.step2.title: Material Mixing
guide.step2.description: Open TC101 bucket and stir thoroughly with a mixer or stick. Material is ready to use – do not thin with water or other additives. If material is too thick, let it warm to room temperature (20–25 °C) and stir again.
guide.step3.title: Application Method
guide.step3.description: For small areas, use a brush or roller. For large applications, we recommend airless spray equipment with 0.43–0.53 mm (17–21 thou) tip and 150–200 bar pressure. Apply evenly, without drips or runs. Follow application direction according to surface character (along pipes, in drainage direction on roofs).
guide.step4.title: Layer Thickness and Consumption
guide.step4.description: Apply maximum 0.5 mm per coat (consumption approx. 0.34 kg/m²). For greater thickness, apply multiple coats. Total thickness depends on purpose: burn protection 1–2 mm (2–4 coats), thermal insulation 2–4 mm (4–8 coats). Allow drying time between coats.
guide.step5.title: Drying and Curing Time
guide.step5.description: At 24 °C, coating is dry to touch in 1 hour. Apply next coat in 2–4 hours, once previous is completely dry (shouldn't smear). Full cure takes 24–48 hours. In cold (below 10 °C), drying slows. Do not apply below 5 °C or in humid conditions.
guide.step6.title: Tool Cleaning
guide.step6.description: TC101 is water-based – clean tools with water immediately after use. Wash brushes and rollers in warm soapy water. Flush spray equipment with water according to manufacturer instructions. Dried material is difficult to remove – don't wait to clean.
